prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this tunable moire system

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a rare case in which a specific, checkable theoretical prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, with the bandwidth collapsing at a magic twist angle) was followed by a specific experimental discovery (correlated insulators and superconductivity in the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 devices), and the two are tied together by a single control parameter. That clean theory-to-experiment line gives a natural three-person configuration within the supplied credit. Opening ballots show broad agreement on the substance: seven of eight members ranked it, and Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson all describe the same prediction-plus-experiment pairing. The downstream impact is large, since the same idea now operates in graphene multilayers, transition-metal dichalcogenides and rhombohedral stacks, and it created a platform on which flat-band and correlation physics can be tuned electrostatically. As an electronic-structure theorist I also value that computed band structure and measured transport meet so directly here.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is that the field is only about eight years old and the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so a prize now could be seen as early; Lindroth and Mehlig make this point. Attribution is also imperfect: Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 experiments, and other groups on moire devices (Dean, Young, Kim, Yacoby, Efetov), fall outside the three supplied names, and earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theory complicates strict priority for the flat-band idea. Finally, its two-sided support is not a majority first-place support; the optical lattice clock candidate B001 has stronger opening backing and fewer attribution problems.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B017 low because the interpretation of the superconducting state is unsettled and recognition may be somewhat early, while she ranks the optical lattice clock first as a stable, confirmed result.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously, but I would separate the discovery from the interpretation. What is secure and replicated across many groups is the existence of the flat bands, the correlated insulating states and the superconducting domes as functions of twist angle and gate voltage; the pairing mechanism is a downstream question, much as the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity did not prevent recognition of its discovery. I also grant that B001 is the cleaner case on attribution and I would not oppose it, but I do not accept that an open microscopic mechanism makes B017 premature, given the replication and the breadth of follow-on platforms.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the optical lattice clock first as a clean instrument-driven advance with two natural laureates, independent confirmation in several laboratories and a pending redefinition of the second, and does not rank B017.
responses.response: I agree that B001 has the tidier attribution and strong laboratory confirmation, and that is why I list it as my first alternative. Where I disagree is on what is weighed against it: the clocks refine a measurement capability whose conceptual basis (frequency-comb metrology, laser cooling, trapping) is already recognised by earlier prizes, whereas twisted bilayer graphene opened a new class of correlated matter and a new control knob. I would not say Kroll's choice is wrong, only that for a committee wanting a discovery of a new regime of matter I find B017 more compelling, and its omission from Kroll's ballot leaves me unsure whether the objection is scientific or about maturity.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B017 first, as a concrete prediction followed by a specific experiment, but notes that credit to junior experimental co-authors and to other groups is unresolved.
responses.response: I agree with the ranking and with the caution. Cao as first author and the broader moire device community are exactly the weak point, and I think the committee should be candid that the three-person limit forces a choice that cannot reflect everyone; the group-leader convention is defensible but not beyond criticism. I would not extend the prize to cover related fractional Chern insulators or other moire discoveries, which Johansson rightly says may need separate recognition later.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B017 second and B015 third, valuing a decisive experiment and a materials-driven discovery in which interface and crystal structure decide the physics, but sees attribution for B015 as only partly resolved.
responses.response: We agree on B015 as a serious candidate, and I ranked it third myself because the coherent MgO tunnelling picture is a good match between first-principles theory and experiment. But I share her attribution worry more strongly than my opening ballot suggested: omission of Yuasa, Djayaprawira and the theorists Butler and Mathon makes the three-name configuration for B015 harder to defend than B017, and the 2007 GMR prize covers part of the conceptual ground. That is why I keep B015 as an alternative rather than my preferred choice.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the unresolved pairing mechanism as a maturity problem or as a separate question from the discovery.
Whether the three-name limit can be defended given Cao and other experimental contributors outside the supplied credit.
Whether B017 or B001 would attract broader agreement; opening support favours B001 and I have not resolved how much that should count.
My recollection of twisted-bilayer history and priority is from memory and not verified against sources.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My own research in electronic structure, DFT and magnetism is adjacent to B017, B015 and B012, which is a matter of familiarity rather than a documented personal or institutional tie to any credited person.
